quote.translation: C. I. Lewis (C. I. Lewis, A Survey of Symbolic Logic, 1918, p. 293, 312) (see p. 193) calls the property common to apodicticity (see p. 198), that is, to impossibility (~) and necessity (~-), "strict implication" (Strict Implication), and the property common to assertoricity, that is, to truth ( ) and falsity (-), "material implication" (Material Implication); and he calls the property common to problematicity, that is, to possibility (-~) and contingency (-~-), "consistency" (Consistency).

regions.text: ）と云つてゐるが、「厳密包含」を表はすにはんの記號を用ひ、「質料包含を表はすには口の記號を用ひ、「煎立」を表はすには〇の記跳を用ひてるる。

quote.translation: To express "strict implication" he uses the sign ⥽, to express "material implication" the sign ⊃, and to express "consistency" the sign ○.

regions.text: 煎立とは甲をことが雨立し得る性質を云つてゐるので、甲であることも可能であり、甲でないことも可能甲は偶然である場合を指してゐるのである。

quote.translation: Consistency means the property by which A and B can stand together, and refers to the case in which it is possible that something is A and also possible that it is not A, that is, in which A is contingent.

quote.translation: p ○ q expresses -~p (p is possible) or -~-p (it is possible that not p, which is to say that p is contingent).

regions.text: Pとqこの開係をOで表はしてゐるのはpかqかいづれになるかが不確定のまま間題として残されてゐることを示してゐる。

quote.translation: That the relation between p and q is represented by ○ shows that whether things will turn out p or q is left open as a problem, undetermined.

quote.translation: Whether the "ball" symbolised by ○ will roll towards p or towards q is wholly uncertain.

quote.translation: Its character is entirely different from that of "material implication", expressed by the hammer shape ⊃, or of "strict implication", expressed by the anchor shape ⥽.

regions.text: 斯やうに記號的論理學でOが間題性の象徴となつてゐるのはギリシア人が女神ラ、ケの持物に「球」を選んだのと全く同

quote.translation: That ○ has become in this way the symbol of problematicity in symbolic logic rests on exactly the same psychology as the Greeks' choice of the "ball" as an attribute of the goddess Tychē.

quote.translation: Of the three modes of hypothetical contingency, the contingency of ground concerns the so-called "ground of knowledge", and so belonged purely to the range of logic.
